_doc:
THE LIST-MARKER HALF OF `text_layout_paragraph` -- and the reason it is a SEPARATE family from the verb of that name. The `text_layout_paragraph` verb drives `text_layout::layout_with_paragraphs`; it never reaches the module called text_layout_paragraph. Those functions (`marker_text`, `to_alpha`, `to_roman`, `compute_counters`) are called only from the RENDERER -- jas_dioxus/src/canvas/render.rs and JasSwift/Sources/Canvas/CanvasSubwindow.swift -- so every bulleted and numbered list an artist draws went through arithmetic that no corpus family watched.

The fifth function, `build_segments_from_text` / `buildParagraphSegments`, is NOT here: it consumes a tspan list and a content string, which is the text corpus's shape rather than this one's, and giving it a home is a separate vector set. That is a declared omission, not an oversight.

EXPECTATIONS ARE HAND-DERIVED from PARAGRAPH.md's enumeration and from the definitions of spreadsheet base-26 and Roman numerals. Comparison is EXACT: every answer is a string or an integer, and a tolerance would mean nothing.

vectors.name: marker_bullet_disc
vectors.derivation: PARAGRAPH.md maps bullet-disc to U+2022 BULLET, and the counter is ignored for every bullet-* style -- passing 7 must change nothing.

vectors.name: marker_bullet_open_square
vectors.derivation: bullet-open-square is U+25A1 WHITE SQUARE, not U+25A0 BLACK SQUARE. The pair separates the two square styles, which are one codepoint apart and easy to transpose.

vectors.name: marker_bullet_square
vectors.derivation: The other half of that pair: bullet-square is U+25A0 BLACK SQUARE.

vectors.name: marker_num_decimal
vectors.derivation: num-decimal renders the counter followed by a period. The trailing '.' is part of the marker, not something the renderer adds.

vectors.name: marker_num_lower_alpha_past_z
vectors.derivation: Counter 27 is the first two-letter marker: base-26 with no zero digit gives 'aa', so the marker is 'aa.'. This is the one value that separates spreadsheet base-26 from ordinary base-26, in which 27 would be 'ba'.

vectors.name: marker_num_upper_roman
vectors.derivation: 1990 = M + CM + XC, so the upper-roman marker is 'MCMXC.'. It exercises both subtractive pairs.

vectors.name: marker_unknown_style_is_empty
vectors.derivation: DEGENERATE, and it is a contract rather than an accident: an unrecognised style returns the EMPTY string so the renderer skips drawing a marker. A port that returned the style name, or the bare counter, would draw garbage into the artboard.

vectors.name: alpha_one_is_a
vectors.derivation: The counter is 1-BASED: 1 maps to 'a', not to 'b' and not to the empty string.

vectors.name: alpha_twenty_six_is_z
vectors.derivation: 26 is the last single letter. n -= 1 gives 25, 25 % 26 = 25 -> 'z', and 25 / 26 = 0 terminates.

vectors.name: alpha_fifty_two_is_az
vectors.derivation: SEPARATES THE TWO DIGITS, which 'aa' cannot. n=52: 51 % 26 = 25 -> 'z', 51/26 = 1; then 0 -> 'a'. Reversed: 'az'. Uppercase gives 'AZ'.

vectors.name: alpha_fifty_three_carries_to_ba
vectors.derivation: The step after 'AZ' must be 'BA', not 'AA' and not 'BZ'. n=53: 52 % 26 = 0 -> 'a', 52/26 = 2; then 1 % 26 = 1 -> 'b'. Reversed: 'ba' -> 'BA'.

vectors.name: alpha_zero_is_empty
vectors.derivation: DEGENERATE: there is no zeroth letter in a system with no zero digit, so 0 returns the empty string rather than looping or underflowing.

vectors.name: roman_one
vectors.derivation: 1 = I, lowercased to 'i'.

vectors.name: roman_four_is_subtractive
vectors.derivation: 4 must be 'iv', not 'iiii'. This is the smallest subtractive pair.

vectors.name: roman_nine_is_subtractive
vectors.derivation: 9 must be 'ix', not 'viiii'. Paired with 4 above, the two pin both of the units-place subtractive forms.

vectors.name: roman_thirty_nine_ninety_nine_is_the_ceiling
vectors.derivation: 3999 is the largest standard Roman numeral: MMM + CM + XC + IX = MMMCMXCIX. It exercises every subtractive pair in one value.

vectors.name: roman_above_the_ceiling_falls_back_to_parentheses
vectors.derivation: DEGENERATE, and it is a documented contract: standard Roman tops out at MMMCMXCIX, so 4000 collapses to the parenthesised decimal '(4000)' -- in BOTH cases, upper and lower, since there is nothing to case. A port that emitted 'MMMM' would disagree here and nowhere else.

vectors.name: roman_zero_is_empty
vectors.derivation: DEGENERATE: Roman numerals have no zero, so 0 returns the empty string.

vectors.name: counters_run_breaks_on_a_bullet_and_restarts
vectors.derivation: PARAGRAPH.md counter-run rule. Two num-decimal paragraphs count 1, 2. A bullet paragraph is not a numbered list, so it takes 0 AND BREAKS THE RUN. The next num-decimal therefore restarts at 1 rather than continuing at 3 -- that restart is the whole content of the rule. The two num-lower-roman paragraphs then start their own run at 1 and 2, because a DIFFERENT num- style also breaks the run.

vectors.name: counters_a_styleless_paragraph_breaks_the_run
vectors.derivation: A paragraph with NO list style at all (null, not a bullet) breaks the run exactly as a bullet does, so the interleaving gives [0,1,0,1] and never [0,1,0,2].

vectors.name: counters_empty_input_is_empty
vectors.derivation: DEGENERATE: no paragraphs, no counters. Pinned so that a port returning [0] for the empty case is caught.
